target.name: Nominal
target.founder: Cameron McCord, Bryce Strauss, Jason Hoch

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in AI & Software. Range: $2.0B - $3.8B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Nominal is a Series B-2 stage AI & Software company currently valued at $1.0B, having raised $155M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 same-sector companies in the similar valuation tier, spanning stages from Series B through IPO, with a broader reference universe of 9 peers total (1 public, 8 private).

The peer-median method, the sole applicable triangulation approach given available data, identifies a median valuation of $3.2B across the comparables. The three direct peers—Ayar Labs at $3.8B (Series E), Black Forest Labs at $3.2B (Series B), and Field AI at $2.0B (IPO)—establish a range of $2.0B to $3.8B. This methodologically supports an implied valuation of $3.2B.

The triangulated range, derived from the peer-median approach, indicates a valuation corridor of $2.8B (low) to $3.7B (high), with a median of $3.2B. This implies meaningful upside from the current $1.0B valuation. Key uncertainties include the limited depth of the peer set (n=3), mixed stage heterogeneity among comparables, and reliance on a single valuation method. The IPO-stage comparability of Field AI also introduces timing and market-condition volatility. Further analysis incorporating revenue multiples or growth-rate adjustments would strengthen conviction in any point estimate within the $2.8B–$3.7B band.
